answer: A broker moving copper from a river depot to a ridge workshop makes each bidding agent solve a fresh sequential delay puzzle bound to that shipment and its public key. The broker checks the proof cheaply and accepts one bid per solution; copying it to another account fails. A Sybil operator may still submit many bids, but must spend compute time and electricity for every one, so extra names alone confer no advantage. Rich operators with faster hardware can still crowd out smaller agents, so the market should cap bids per round and offer a slower low-cost lane.
